obtained.how: USDA Forest Service FishXing project's open reference library (agency web page), scan with a text layer

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the article's title page and running heads
bibliography.note: Ecology 34(2): 347–365, April 1953 (printed page = PDF page + 346). Shelby D. Gerking, Department of Zoology, Indiana University.

claims.quote: two main pool areas separated by a shallow riffle, 242 feet long
claims.conditions: Richland Creek, a bedrock stream in Greene County, Indiana; the riffle (section D) was chosen in the expectation that it would be a mechanical barrier

claims.claim: in Indiana only 2 of 19 smallmouth bass crossed a 74-m riffle in four years
claims.source_value: 2 of 19 recaptures of fin-clipped smallmouth bass crossed the long riffle (Table VI, recaptures during four years)
claims.location: p. 355 (PDF p. 9), text and Table VI
claims.quote: only 2 of 19 recaptures crossed the long riffle
claims.conditions: Richland Creek, Indiana, 1948–1951; marked smallmouth 106–305 mm fork length (mean 179 mm); electric-shocker mark–recapture
claims.note: Context the paper's 'sedentary' gloss leaves out: Gerking concluded the smallmouth 'has a home range about twice as great as the other sunfishes' (6 of 11 recaptures in the downstream pool had strayed between its sections), and in the 1951 sample 3 of 4 bass recaptured after several years had crossed the riffle to the upstream pool (p. 358). In Stott's Creek all 7 recaptures (of 21 marked) were where they were marked.

claims.claim: over four years only 5 of 191 recaptured longear sunfish crossed the 74-m riffle
claims.source_value: 5 of 191 recoveries crossed the long riffle during the four years
claims.location: p. 352 (PDF p. 6), text and Table III
claims.quote: Only 5 of the 191 recoveries moved across the long intervening riffle
claims.conditions: Richland Creek, Indiana, 1948–1951; longears of ages II–V(VI); most found within 100–200 ft of where marked

claims.claim: 26 of 35 transplanted longears went back across the riffle within two weeks
claims.source_value: 26 of 35 RECAPTURED transplanted longears were back in their home section B two weeks after transplanting (18 of 29 at six weeks); 55 newly marked longears plus 6 marked in an earlier year were transplanted (Table X)
claims.location: p. 359 (PDF p. 13), text and Table XI; p. 358 (PDF p. 12), Table X
claims.quote: Twenty-six of 35 RP recaptures were taken in section B two weeks after
claims.conditions: Experiment III, Richland Creek, 1951: section B (downstream pool) emptied of fish and its fish moved upstream across the riffle into section E
claims.note: The 35 are recaptures, not the number transplanted (about 61). Say '26 of 35 recaptured transplanted longears'.

claims.claim: a riffle can act as 'a behavioral rather than a mechanical barrier' (quotation)
claims.source_value: the transplant result 'indicated that the riffle was a behavioral rather than a mechanical barrier'
claims.quote: the riffle was a behavioral rather than a mechanical barrier

notes: Also usable: Gerking estimated that marked-fish loss from the study area was no more than about 5 % of recaptures (17 of 80 strays crossed the long riffle, p. 351); rock bass and golden redhorse were also restricted (golden redhorse: 4 of 28 recaptures crossed the riffle); spotted bass, like smallmouth, had about twice the sunfishes' range (1 of 16 crossed). Home range here is the 100–200 ft scale for sunfishes.
